fixes.explanation: Weapons do show up in the song, friend, but not as the reason. God's arrows and sword come up later (Deuteronomy 32:23; 32:41; 32:42). Here Moses asks how one could chase a thousand "…unless their Rock had sold them, unless the LORD had given them up?" (Deuteronomy 32:30). The way the question is built, it happens only if the LORD had given them up.

The song says, "He abandoned the God who made him and scorned the Rock of his salvation." (Deuteronomy 32:15). Just before that, Jeshurun is "…fat, bloated, and gorged." You know that feeling after a whole tray of cookies, when all you want is a nap? Jeshurun got that full, and instead of a nap, he walked out on God.

Altar's a fair guess, friend, but this verse heads somewhere else. God says, "…I will make them jealous by those who are not a people; I will make them angry by a nation without understanding." (Deuteronomy 32:21). I think that would sting, like getting outbaked by a bowl of plain flour that never met an oven.

problems.problem: It uses a dash. No em dashes or en dashes.
The explanation repeats that God made Jeshurun, then adds a flat comparison about Papa never saying goodbye to his own Maker. It feels moralizing rather than fatherly or engaging.
The explanation is flat and repetitive: it quotes the answer, repeats it, and twice notes that altars are absent without adding a distinct Papa Dorin voice.
